sub_branches.concept_or_rule: Raw Data vs Organized Frequency Tables
step_by_step_procedure: Raw Data: Unorganized initial list of facts or observations.
Organize raw data into categories.
Count occurrences per category to determine frequency.
formulas_and_identities: Frequency = Integer count of observations in a category

step_by_step_procedure: Record observations using vertical strokes '|'.
Draw 4 vertical strokes for first 4 counts ('||||').
Cross diagonally with 5th stroke to complete bundle ('||||/').
Sum bundles (5s) and individual strokes.
Select a simple, clear picture icon.
Declare a key scale defining how many units 1 icon represents.
Calculate icon count per category = Category Frequency / Scale Key.
formulas_and_identities: Icon Count = Category Frequency / Key Scale Unit
sub_branches.example_problem: Scale: 1 bicycle icon = 6 bikes. For 42 bikes: 42 / 6 = 7 icons.

step_by_step_procedure: Draw horizontal axis (X-axis for categories) and vertical axis (Y-axis for frequencies).
Vertical axis scale MUST start at 0.
Draw rectangular bars of uniform width.
Maintain equal spacing gaps between adjacent bars.
formulas_and_identities: Bar Height (cm) = Frequency / Quantity represented per cm
sub_branches.example_problem: Frequency = Rs 3200, Scale: 1 cm = Rs 400. Bar Height = 3200 / 400 = 8 cm.

step_by_step_procedure: Compare bar heights to identify highest/lowest categories.
Calculate category sum totals and percentage proportions.
Formulate comparative ratios.
formulas_and_identities: Category Percentage = (Category Frequency / Total Frequency) x 100

step_by_step_procedure: Inspect vertical axis starting point.
If axis starts above 0 (truncated axis), bar height ratios distort real proportions.
Re-plot with 0-baseline to ensure visual accuracy.
sub_branches.example_problem: Bar heights of 100 and 110 look 10x taller if axis starts at 99. Fixed by starting at 0.
